MATERIAL: the A&R states 'Monthly principal is 0.10%' without naming its base. The borrower's certified Covenant Calculation exhibits (2026-Q1, 2026-Q2 -- part of the same lender compliance-certificate package) compute this as 0.10% of the PRIOR month's OUTSTANDING (declining) balance -- verified to the penny for 2026-04 ($51,000.00 = 0.10% x $51,000,000.00), 2026-05 ($50,949.00 = 0.10% x $50,949,000.00) and 2026-06 ($50,898.05 = 0.10% x $50,898,051.00), tying exactly to the Approved Stabilization Budget's 'Ending debt' column. This debt-service engine (v1) only supports a FLAT annual percentage of the ORIGINAL aggregate funded principal (the base is invariant absent a new draw), so it structurally CANNOT reproduce a declining-balance amortization. This spec approximates the contractual amortization as a flat 1.2%/12 of the original $51,000,000.00 combined principal ($51,000.00/month, every month to maturity). Compare the generated schedule's monthly principal to the certified Covenant Calculation figures each quarter -- the flat approximation will diverge from the true declining-balance schedule starting with the second installment (May 2026) and the gap compounds toward maturity (2031-03-31); reconcile against the certified exhibits rather than relying on the generated schedule standalone, and consider populating covenant_support_rows.scheduled_principal directly from certified data if the gap becomes material to a live covenant.

VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE GENERATOR (--as-of 2026-06): the generated schedule's cash interest is 424,575.00 (2026-04), 438,288.33 (2026-05), 423,725.00 (2026-06) against the certified 425,000.00 / 424,575.00 / 424,150.43 for the same months -- not a match in any of the three months, and NOT explained solely by the declining-balance issue above. Comparing the certified figures directly: 425,000.00 = $51,000,000.00 x 10%/12 exactly; 424,575.00 = $50,949,000.00 x 10%/12 exactly; 424,150.43 = $50,898,051.00 x 10%/12 (rounded). I.e. the certified interest calculation is a FLAT annual-rate-divided-by-12 convention applied to the BEGINNING-of-month (pre-that-month's-own-principal-payment) balance, with NO variation for the actual number of calendar days in the month (April=30, May=31, June=30) -- effectively a 30/360 bond-basis 'even month' convention. This debt-service engine (v1) only supports 'actual/360' or 'actual/365' with REAL calendar-day counting (so its interest necessarily varies between a 30-day and a 31-day month, as seen in the 424,575.00 -> 438,288.33 -> 423,725.00 generated series), and has no 'flat annual/12, no day-count' or true '30/360 bond-basis' option -- this is a SEPARATE engine capability gap from the declining-balance issue above, not a spec-tuning error. actual/360 with count_both_endpoints=true was kept as the closest available approximation (it alone reproduces the certified figure for a month that happens to be exactly 30 days, e.g. April or June, when also using the correct pre-payment balance) but the generated monthly cash-interest figures should NOT be relied on standalone -- reconcile every month against the certified Covenant Calculation / Compliance Certificate exhibits, and treat this as an open engine-enhancement item (a 30/360 bond-basis day-count option) for a future revision of debt_service.py.
